title: Request for Information (RFI) / Containerized Payload Capabilities
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Containerized Payload Capabilities 1. PURPOSE The Department of the Navy (DON), Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research regarding containerized payload capabilities. The purpose of this RFI is to: Identify the realm of the possible for containerized payload capabilities that will provide operational utility to the Fleet; and Characterize the physical, electrical, data, communications, thermal, and other interfaces required by those capabilities to inform future approaches for simplifying payload integration across Naval afloat / ashore enterprise. The Government is intentionally not prescribing specific payload capabilities or detailed performance requirements through this RFI. DRPM RAS seeks industry�s perspective on what is possible, including capabilities the Government may not currently be considering. The Government is interested in existing products, adaptations of existing technologies, and technically feasible concepts that could be demonstrated, produced affordably, and delivered at scale on an accelerated timeline. Information obtained through this RFI will inform Fleet engagement, budgeting, experimentation, demonstrations, prize challenges, prototyping efforts, follow-on market research, requirements development, and potential future acquisition activities. 2. BACKGROUND Robotic and autonomous systems have the potential to increase the reach, persistence, capacity, and distribution of naval capabilities while reducing risk to personnel and high-value platforms. The Department of the Navy is pursuing opportunities to accelerate the development, integration, acquisition, and fielding of RAS capabilities responsive to Fleet operational needs. A key opportunity is the ability to rapidly add, exchange, and scale mission capabilities without requiring each payload to be designed around a single purpose-built platform. Containerized payloads may provide a means to separate mission capability from the underlying host platform, enabling the DON to more rapidly integrate new technologies, interchange capabilities among suitable platforms, and increase operational capacity through distributed employment at scale. DRPM RAS is therefore seeking industry�s perspective on the breadth of capabilities that could be delivered in a containerized form factor. The Government seeks to understand not only what is commercially or operationally available today, but also what could reasonably be adapted, developed, or demonstrated on an accelerated timeline. The Government also seeks to better understand the host-platform interfaces and services required to support a broad range of containerized capabilities. Understanding common requirements for power, data, communications, thermal management, mechanical interfaces, and other services�as well as existing commercial, maritime, and military interface standards�may enable the Government to simplify future integration and reduce platform-specific engineering. DRPM RAS intends to use the information received to develop a broad portfolio of potential capabilities for consideration by Fleet stakeholders. Fleet interest may subsequently inform more focused technical exchanges, RFIs, demonstrations, prototyping activities, requirements development, and acquisition efforts. Of particular interest are capabilities that can be produced affordably and at scale on an accelerated timeline, with the objective of enabling delivery of meaningful quantities. 3. DESIRED CHARACTERISTICS / GUARDRAILS The Government is particularly interested in containerized payload concepts that, to the greatest extent practicable: Utilize a standard 20-foot and/or 40-foot ISO container form factor; Are platform agnostic, minimizing platform-specific integration and enabling employment from multiple suitable host platforms; Support remote operation and Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA)/open interfaces, as applicable; Are capable of being produced affordably and employed at scale; and Are available today or could reasonably be demonstrated, produced, and delivered on an accelerated timeline. These characteristics are intended to guide, rather than unnecessarily constrain, industry responses. Respondents should not exclude a potentially valuable capability solely because it does not meet every desired characteristic. Significant deviations, limitations, or host-platform dependencies should instead be identified in the response. The maritime operating environment (afloat and ashore) should be considered the baseline for proposed concepts and interfaces. 4. INFORMATION REQUESTED Respondents are invited to identify one or more containerized payload capability concepts that could provide operational value to the Fleet. The Government encourages respondents to submit multiple concepts and prioritizes breadth of relevant ideas over detailed engineering descriptions at this stage. For each capability concept, provide the following information: 4.1 Capability / Operational Effect Briefly describe: The proposed capability; The operational effect or mission function it enables; and How the capability could provide value when employed from a robotic, autonomous, or other maritime platform or shore site. Respondents are specifically encouraged to identify capabilities that the Government may not currently be considering. Concepts are not limited to currently fielded products. Respondents may identify existing capabilities, adaptations of existing technologies, developmental capabilities, or technically feasible concepts that could reasonably be matured within the Government�s desired timeframe. 4.2 Host-Platform Interfaces / Umbilicals Identify the interfaces and services required from the host platform to operate the proposed capability. As applicable, provide: Electrical power: AC/DC, voltage, phase/frequency, continuous and peak power requirements; Data: required interfaces/protocols, approximate bandwidth, and physical medium such as copper or fiber; Communications/RF: external antenna, RF, SATCOM, PNT/GPS, or other connectivity requirements; Thermal management: ventilation, cooling, chilled water, or other heat-rejection requirements; Mechanical/physical interfaces: mounting or other significant physical integration requirements; Grounding and bonding requirements; Other services: fuel, fluids, compressed air, seawater, drainage, exhaust, or other external services, as applicable; and Any additional connection or equipment external to the container required for operation of the capability. Where applicable, identify existing commercial, maritime, military, or other industry-standard connectors, interfaces, protocols, or specifications currently used or recommended for these connections. Respondents are encouraged to identify interface approaches that minimize host-platform modification and facilitate rapid installation, removal, replacement, and interchange of containerized payloads in a maritime environment. 4.3 Maturity / Availability Identify whether the capability: Is available or demonstrable today; Requires adaptation or integration of existing technology; or Requires additional development. Provide the earliest date at which a representative capability could be demonstrated and, if different, the earliest date at which production units could reasonably begin delivery. Detailed Technology Readiness Level documentation is not requested. 4.4 Container / Physical Footprint Identify whether the capability can reasonably be accommodated within a standard: 20-foot ISO container; 40-foot ISO container Identify significant external components, topside equipment, or other installation requirements, if applicable. Approximate payload weight and significant size/weight limitations should be provided if known. 4.5 Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Cost Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost for the proposed capabi

Award Notice - MOUTH OF THE COLUMBIA RIVER - NORTH JETTY MAJOR MAINTENANCE - PHASE II -
description: This award announcement is for the North Jetty Major Maintenance � Phase II, Klickitat County, Washington. The MCR federal navigation project is situated at the border between Washington and Oregon, where the Columbia River meets the Pacific Ocean. Deep-draft navigation through the MCR is facilitated by three primary navigation structures-North Jetty, South Jetty, and Jetty A-with a combined authorized length of 10.2 miles. The North Jetty has an authorized length of 2.5 miles extending to Station 130+00; however, it has not been constructed to its full authorized length. The initial construction of the North Jetty concluded at approximately Station 122+00, resulting in a constructed length of approximately 2.3 miles. This jetty was the second of the three to be constructed and was completed in 1917. Subsequent repairs and rehabilitations along various sections of the North Jetty were carried out in 1939, 1965, 2005, 2015, and 2019. Both initial construction and repairs utilized stone with a minimum density ranging from 167 to 180 pounds per cubic foot (pd). The side slopes of the jetty vary between 1:1.25 and 1:2 (vertical: horizontal), with an average crest elevation of 25 ft msl. Since construction, a total of 3,569,030 tons of armor stone have been placed. The Mouth of the Columbia River (MCR) North Jetty is located at the southwest corner of Washington State near Ilwaco, WA. Access to the north jetty is from N Head Rd and Cape Disappointment State Park. Mandatory work for MCR North Jetty Expedited Repairs includes toe, side slope, and crest repair construction above -5 feet NAVD88 elevation along approximately 900 feet of the jetty trunk primarily on the ocean side. These sections will be repaired and reconstructed to a design crest width of 30 feet, side slopes of 1V:2H and a crest elevation of +24.5 feet NAVD88. The estimated stone volume required for the repairs is approximately 11,100 cubic yards with an approximate minimum stone densities of 185 pounds per cubic foot. Expected stone size is between 20-40 tons each. A jetty crest haul road on top of the jetty must be constructed and staging area developed to store the large quantity of jetty armor stone.
